attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his own post, in his own voice.

semantics.note: Keeps the named systems and the 'looked at them carefully' qualifier. 'Nobody' may be rhetorical, but it still asserts a present-tense judgment about careful observers.

contract.note: Reading 'human intelligence' as broad, flexible intelligence rather than performance on one task is the ordinary reading. Requiring evidence of agreement among careful observers matches the 'nobody' wording. The window from April to May 14, 2022 is reasonable.

evidence.note: Flamingo paper (April 2022) documents hallucinations and ungrounded guesses. That shows limits, but not how careful observers judged the system or a comparison with broad human intelligence.

Peer-reviewed analysis from May 2022 credits GPT-3 with some semantic ability but flags unreliable truth-telling. It does not claim human equivalence, so it neither contradicts nor establishes the claim.

reviews.rationale: Neither item shows a careful evaluator treating these systems as broadly human-level, so nothing contradicts the claim. But nothing establishes the asserted agreement among careful observers or a comparison with human intelligence covering all four systems. The packet's own stated gaps say the same.

attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his own post.

semantics.note: Faithful, including the weaker 'in no way guarantees'. The guarantee point is a logical caution and 'inductive folly' is evaluative. The checkable core is the historical claim that the failure modes persist, and the contract correctly scores only that.

contract.note: Reading 'have not changed' as the same kinds of failure persisting, not identical error rates, is the ordinary reading of a claim about failure modes. It is neither stretched for nor against him. The guarantee and folly remarks are rightly left unscored.

evidence.note: Fodor and Pylyshyn (1988) set out the systematicity (compositionality) critique. It is the historical baseline, not evidence about 2022 systems.
Pinker and Prince (1988) list failures of the RM model, including errors and missing outputs. Historical baseline only.
April 2022 study: compositional generalization on SCAN and RobustFill remains challenging even for modified Transformers. That is direct evidence the compositionality failures persisted.

PaLM report (April 2022): semantic-understanding errors, hallucinations and symbol-mapping errors persist, though scaling fixed many. This supports persistence of the failure kinds, not unchanged error rates.

2018 revisit says many of Pinker and Prince's specific past-tense objections are resolved. That cuts against a literal reading, but under the contract fixes to particular tasks do not contradict persistence of the failure kinds.

reviews.rationale: The 1988 critiques identify systematicity and linguistic-generalization failures. Research available by May 2022 (e3, e4) documents compositional failures, semantic misunderstanding and hallucination-type unreliability in current neural systems. Specific fixes (e5, the improvements in e4) count only as particular-task progress under the contract. On the fair reading that the same kinds of failure persist, the claim holds; the stronger reading of unchanged deficiencies would not.

attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his own post.

semantics.note: Keeps 'virtually all' and 'still depends'. Dropping the examples and the evaluative 'Sutton sells that short' leaves the factual core intact.

contract.note: In context (Flash Fill rests on classical programming techniques, contrasted with Big Data), reading knowledge engineering as deliberately programmed logic is what an informed reader would take. 'Virtually all' as nearly universal across software categories is ordinary.

evidence.note: Chromium documentation from May 2022 shows explicitly coded security policies in one browser. It is one example and a project disclosure, not a measure of software worldwide.
LibreOffice 7.3.3 announcement mentions document-conversion libraries. It is one example and a project disclosure; it does not establish how widespread the dependence is.

reviews.rationale: The packet has two single-product disclosures that fit the broad reading but cannot establish nearly universal dependence across the world's software. No representative survey was found, and nothing contradicts the claim. The evidence does not settle it.

attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his own post.

semantics.note: Keeps 'so far', 'most but not all' and 'for now' as limits on scope and time. It is a historical observation, not a forecast.

contract.note: In context (Sutton's Bitter Lesson), reading this as AI application domains with better demonstrated performance is the ordinary reading. Allowing exceptions respects his own 'not all'.

evidence.note: AlphaZero (2017) beat the hand-engineered Stockfish at chess. That is one domain win and cannot establish a majority of domains.
AI Index 2022 abstract is relevant to breadth across AI but gives no domain-by-domain comparison, so it settles nothing.

reviews.rationale: The packet contains one selected domain example and a survey abstract without domain-level comparisons. No defensible comparison across domains establishes or refutes that data-driven methods led in most AI domains by May 2022. The evidence does not settle it.
